paragraph: On the random panel (110 codes, 179,830 reports, test prevalence 0.027, 22 recall events), all methods scored lower. Narrative evidence again improved on count evidence (AUPRC 0.034 vs 0.022; difference 0.013, 0.001 to 0.030; AUROC 0.59 vs 0.43) but did not beat PRR (AUPRC 0.039) or recall history (0.125; AUROC 0.81). Generic retrieval was worse than full reading, and AEGIS did not improve on generic retrieval (Supplementary Table S6).
abstract: In 110 randomly sampled codes (prevalence 0.027) the ordering held; recall history remained strongest (AUPRC 0.13).
rows: GBM, count + recall history + narrative features
Fusion + full reading, initial reports only
note: 110 of 900 randomly drawn product codes met the eligibility rule (≥24 reports received in 2014–2015); 20 had a Class I recall. 179,830 sampled reports (up to 30 per code-month). Test period July 2022–June 2025: 3,858 cases, 103 positive (prevalence 0.027), 22 recall events. Events detected: share of the 21 evaluable test-period recall events with at least one alert in the 6 months before initiation, at the threshold set on the validation period as in the main analysis. Leave-one-code-out ΔAUPRC (full reading − count evidence) ranged from 0.008 to 0.015. Bootstrap: 1,000 resamples.
